summary: A satirical piece about small businesses in the fictional town of Cybersville stumbling into digital marketing after a small business seminar on September 3, 2023. Each business, from a cat sweater shop to a garlic stand, a sourdough bakery, a bookstore, a vegan café and a potion shop, botches hashtags, SEO, email campaigns, websites, viral fame or analytics in humorous ways.
one_line: Satirical account of Cybersville's small businesses comically failing at hashtags, SEO, email marketing, websites, viral trends and analytics after a digital seminar.
key_facts: The annual "How Do You Do, Fellow Kids?" small business seminar was held on September 3, 2023 and kicked off Cybersville's digital stumbling.
Mrs. Mildred of Mrs. Mildred's Cat Sweater Emporium posted her first Instagram photo, of Mr. Whiskers in a festive turtleneck, with seventeen hashtags, half of them misspelled.
Bob of Bob's 'All Things Garlic' wrote a blog on September 15, 2023 titled "10 Shocking Benefits of Garlic You Absolutely Must Know!", which suffered from keyword stuffing.

Susan of "Susan's Sourdough and Serenades" began an email marketing campaign on October 5, 2023 with subject lines like "UNBEATABLE DEAL!!!" and novel-length emails about sourdough and interpretive dance.

Kyle, the self-proclaimed "Guru of Growth Hacking," arrived in Cybersville around September 30 and advised businesses to "turn everything into a meme"; rumor held he once ran the till at a defunct video store.
Larry, owner of the bookstore "Read it and Weep," began building a website on September 18, 2023, full of GIFs, animated cursors and the <marquee> tag.
Larry's website took 97 seconds to load each page.
On October 10, 2023, Timmy, a teenage barista at "Green Bean Dreams," accidentally recorded himself slipping on a chickpea, creating the TikTok hit "The 24-Hour Kale Cleanse Dance Challenge."
The café's viral fame was fleeting and sales returned to the usual trickle.
On November 2nd, Peggy of "Peggy's Potent Potions" opened her Google Analytics dashboard and found a 98% bounce rate, which she thought meant people were jumping for joy.
Kyle was last seen trying to explain the ROI of doggo lingo to the local tax attorney.
